### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44c7a4a415a429f3df9daff6bb97701a7f64d416`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44c7a4a415a429f3df9daff6bb97701a7f64d416` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `488a9ee8f8cbf5fce76138cc099a071d69eae406` — the merge of head `7f0c346199f8ed2d2b118b838ad04380a10a81f7` into base `44c7a4a415a429f3df9daff6bb97701a7f64d416`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 488a9ee8f8cbf5fce76138cc099a071d69eae406 && git checkout 488a9ee8f8cbf5fce76138cc099a071d69eae406
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 44c7a4a415a429f3df9daff6bb97701a7f64d416 7f0c346199f8ed2d2b118b838ad04380a10a81f7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 44c7a4a415a429f3df9daff6bb97701a7f64d416 && git merge --no-ff 7f0c346199f8ed2d2b118b838ad04380a10a81f7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44c7a4a415a429f3df9daff6bb97701a7f64d416
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 44c7a4a415a429f3df9daff6bb97701a7f64d416` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Showcase backend (`objectstack dev`, `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1`, fresh SQLite per boot), the real console from this worktree's `ui/` source behind the dev proxy, signed in as the seeded platform admin. **before** = this branch with `pending-sso-users.ts` restored to origin/main 8e498475c (the only source file the PR changes), plugin-auth rebuilt; **after** = head ce3609c51.

| Reading | before (origin/main door) | after (ce3609c51) |
|---|---|---|
| Import Users (CSV, 2 rows), console dialog, `POST /api/v1/actions/sys_user/import_sso_users` | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` "Unknown field(s): organizationId. Send { csv } or { rows }." | 200, summary total 2 · added 2 · failed 0; the Import Finished dialog lists both rows |

Each console call carried the session (Bearer plus the session cookie), recorded per line in readings.txt. Served `/auth/config`: `cloudManaged: true`, `tenancyPosture: single`.

Artefacts (screenshots `before-*` / `after-*`, `readings.txt`, `live-readings.mjs`, `boot.sh`) are in the seat's project folder `objectstack-seat3/34912-live/`.

## Notes

- **Shape.** `Fixes #34912` is in the body. 4 files, +351 −3. `check-governed-merges --pr 34966`: 0 of 4 paths governed, 354 lines, so not Tier H. The seat's fable L2 at the contract tier comes next, as the claim (6956406352) ordered.
- **Surface.** Every changed file is inside the claim surface. `pending-sso-users.ts` and its test file are named. `packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-forward.test.ts` is the "action-execution.ts tests only" leg: it imports `buildApiActionRequest` from `../action-execution.js`, and no runtime source moved. The changeset is in root `.changeset/`. The route wiring was not touched, since `getCallerActiveOrganizationId` was already passed in.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch. That is the only package whose src moved; runtime has a test-only change, so it needs no entry. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` match the claim and the PR body. The widening is real: each door admits one more constrained body key.
- **Scope (seat ruling A).** I read `refuseForeignOrganization` and its three call sites. Each runs right after that door's closed-key check and before any read, write or host call. The body value is compared and then dropped: none of the three doors reads `body.organizationId` after the check. Scope still comes from `deps.getCallerActiveOrganizationId()` and `settleRequest`. Non-string or empty values, a mismatch, and "no active organization" are all refused. Both codes, `INVALID_REQUEST` and `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION`, are already in the ledger. I found no path where the body org reaches scope.
- **Tests.** The 14 `[#34912]` cases cover the full matrix the claim asked for: absent, equal, foreign, no active org, and a no-key control on add. They also cover the bad types on add and the multi-org fake. On the multi-org fake, the join is never called for a foreign org and gets the session value for an equal one. The runtime control proves the generic stamp is unchanged for `import_sso_users`, `add_sso_user` and `ban_user`, and that a caller with no org gets no stamp. The recorded ablation of the equality check turns exactly the four foreign legs red and restores to HEAD.
- **Live readings (6959040633).** These were taken on the showcase with `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1` through the real console, before against after:
  - Import Users: 400 Unknown field became 200, total 2, added 2.
  - Add User: 400 became 200 `idp_pending`, in the session org.
  - Remove with the forwarded body: 400 became 200 `removed: true`.
  - A foreign org on add: 400 naming both orgs, with 0 rows written.
  Screenshots and `readings.txt` are in `objectstack-seat3/34912-live/`.
- **Strings.** No UI strings changed; the door messages are server-side English, as in the rest of the file. No zh/en entries are owed.
- **CI at this head.** Read at the time of this comment: the gates that have finished are green, including Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate and the lint gates. Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates and the Test Core shards were still running. Landing waits on those.
- **Nit (optional, follow-up is fine).** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` lists each door's body keys: about line 1336 for add, 1340 for import and 1414 for remove. It does not mention that a matching `organizationId` is now admitted. A direct API caller loses nothing by omitting it, so this does not block. A one-line docs follow-up would make the widening discoverable.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ce3609c513d20a120fc5c0d5c433cf362ceb7c9d`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. Of the 4 paths, 0 are governed and none is a published schema. The PR body and the changeset both say `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, so the review is owed at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Inputs: the body of card #34912 and every comment on it, including the claim 6956406352 (seat ruling A), the hand-off 6956915503 and the report 6959070737. Also the PR body, the live readings 6959040633, the L1-b ACCEPT 6959151659, the file list, and the net diff against `main` at the head. Code outside the diff was read with `git show` on the head object and was not reviewed. No checkout, no build and no test run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/{add-sso-user, import-sso-users, remove-sso-user}`: widened, correctly.** `unknownBodyKeys` takes exactly one key, `organizationId`, out of each door's unknown set. `refuseForeignOrganization` returns `undefined` as its first statement when that key is not an own property. So a body without the key runs the same code it ran on `main`, and its result does not change. Every body with the key was refused on `main` with `400 INVALID_REQUEST "Unknown field(s): organizationId…"`. Now each of those bodies is either admitted (the value equals the session's active org) or still refused with `400`. **No body that was accepted before is refused now.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right word. This is not a narrowing, so no `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed. For a body that was already refused, only the code and the sentence can change: `INVALID_REQUEST` becomes `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` when the session has no org. The status stays 400. That is not a narrowing either.
- **Can the body org reach scope? No.** At the head, the body value is read only inside `refuseForeignOrganization` (lines 195–214). It is compared, then dropped. Scope comes from these places:
  - the multi-org join: `settleRequest` calls `deps.getCallerActiveOrganizationId()` again (line 338) and hands that value to `joinCurrentOrganization`;
  - single-org: `bindUserToSoleOrganization(deps, userId)` takes no org argument;
  - the audit row: `writeAdminAudit` metadata uses `written.organizationId`, the membership that was actually written;
  - the answer's `organizationId`: `outcome.organizationId`;
  - remove: takes no org at all.

  The multi-org fake test pins this. A foreign org is refused and the join never runs. An equal org is admitted, and the join gets `org_session`, the session's value.
- **Ordering: every refusal comes before any read, write, host call or audit row.** In all three doors the check runs straight after the closed-key check. Before it come only `isCloudManaged()`, the JSON read and the closed-key check, and the route's `gateAdmin` (platform admin) runs before the door. After it come `readPerson`/`settleRequest`/`addOnePendingPerson` and, on remove, `engine.find`, the host and `takeBackPerson`. A session with no active org, or a different org, is refused before any of those. When `getCallerActiveOrganizationId` is not wired, `current` is `null`, so the request is refused (fails closed). It is wired at `auth-plugin.ts:5231`: `authApi.getSession` on the request's own headers.
- **Same session on both sides.** The stamp (`action-execution.ts`, `isIdentityRouteTarget(path) && body.organizationId === undefined && organizationId`) and the door's check both come from the caller's own signed-in session. Per the `isIdentityRouteTarget` jsdoc, the auth mount admits no API key and no OAuth token. If the two ever disagree, the door refuses with 400 naming both orgs. That fails closed, and `main` refused those requests anyway. If an action param sets `organizationId` itself, the stamp does not overwrite it, and the door's equality check is exactly the guard for that case.
- **Refusal shape matches the door's existing refusals.** All three go through the file's own `fail`/`badRequest`, so the body is `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }` with HTTP 400. `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` at 400 is the code and status `settleRequest` already uses on the same door, and `INVALID_REQUEST` is the door's `badRequest`. No new code, so the error-code ledger is unchanged and Lint · docs & code guards is green. The sentences name the org that was sent, the session's org and what was not done. That follows the file's style.
- **Public surface.** Runtime: test-only. `api-action-forward.test.ts` imports `SysUser` from `@objectstack/platform-objects/identity`, which is already a runtime dependency (`package.json:77`) and is already imported by three other runtime tests. No export, spec key or SDK method changed. Metadata authors are not affected, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- **Tests against the ruling's five pins.** The claim (6956406352) asked for five pins, and all are present on the real `AuthManager` and the real route mount:
  - absent key accepted, on all three doors;
  - equal key accepted, ignored for scope, and the person joins `DEFAULT_ORG`. The fixture invariant is asserted before each run;
  - a different org refused, naming both, with nothing written and the host not told;
  - no session org plus a body org refused with `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION`, with a no-key CONTROL on add;
  - the stamp CONTROL in runtime: `import_sso_users`, `add_sso_user` and `ban_user` are still stamped, and a caller with no org gets no stamp.

  Plus the non-string legs (`null`, `''`, `42`). The recorded ablation (`if (sent !== current)` to `if (false)`) turns exactly the four foreign-org legs red.
- **Live readings (6959040633)** on a showcase run with `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1`, before against after. All three doors go from 400 to 200, and a foreign org gets 400 naming both with 0 rows. Those readings were posted, but the console posture they show is `tenancyPosture: single`. The multi-org path is covered only by the fake, which is enough for this face.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`. That is the only package whose `src` moved; runtime has a test-only change and needs no entry. AGENTS.md says a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`, and `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, so the level is right. Both declaration lines start at the beginning of their line in the changeset body and in the PR body, and Check Changeset is green.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — confirmed. Each door admits one more body key, only when it equals the caller's session org. Nothing that was accepted is refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]`, so nothing to answer.
- `security_findings`: `none`. I agree: no path from the body org to scope, membership, a grant, the host event or an audit row.
- Out-of-scope findings in the dev report:
  - the Import Finished result dialog overflows (UX, class a). The PR says it was reported to the seat. The seat should file it if it has not; it does not block this PR.
  - `admin/remove-sso-user` has no declared console action, although the ledger note says Setup → Users posts it. This is an observation only and I agree it does not block.
  - docs drift, covered by the nit below.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation, no in-app join and no new query. `refuseForeignOrganization` makes one session read and touches no data.
- Nit (prose only; the o3-D fold covers it): `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`, near lines 1336, 1340 and 1414, and the `auth-route-ledger.ts:265` note ("body { userId }") describe these door bodies without the now-admitted matching `organizationId`. The review does not change when that fold lands after this head.
- Nit: with multi-org isolation on, the check and `settleRequest` each read the session, so there are two `getSession` calls per request. The test pins `>= 2`. Scope still comes from the second read and the body is never used. Passing the first read into `settleRequest` would save a round-trip. That is optional.
- Nit: the refusal sentence quotes the caller-sent `organizationId` string back with no length limit. It is JSON-encoded and the caller only sees their own input, so there is no injection. A length cap would be tidier.
- Observation, outside the diff, not reviewed: `runRemoveSsoUser` puts no org scope on its target lookup (`sys_user` by id, system context, platform-admin gated). That was so on `main` too. This PR only adds a constraint to that door.
- CI on this head: polled until every check had finished. 37 success, 16 skipped (UI, docs, opt-in and queue-only jobs that do not apply to this diff), 0 failure, 0 cancelled. That includes Test Core (1–10/10) and its aggregate, Type Check · workspace, consumer, source and debt ledger, Build Core, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI and every Lint lane. The PR head is still `ce3609c51` after the poll.

Only nits stay open, which meets the merge standard.
